standard_prerequisites: Field theory: a polynomial of degree < p over a field of characteristic p has nonzero derivative; deg(f') < deg(f) unless f' = 0
core_obligations: If x^p - t = fg, differentiating gives f'g + fg' = 0 with f', g' nonzero (degrees < p) and strictly smaller degree, forcing f and g to share a factor
So any factorization is x^p - t = c f^n with f irreducible and n > 1; since p is prime, n = p and f is linear, which would put a root of x^p - t in F, contradicting the choice of t
proof_roadmap: Derivative argument forces a common factor in any factorization
Prime exponent collapses the factorization to a linear f and a contradiction
